newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent futures end soft after choppy afternoon.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent futures end soft after choppy afternoon.

text.p: IPE Brent Futures ended on a soft note on Wednesday after a choppy afternoon ride with technical selling on NYMEX wiping out early gains and short covering from the bottom of selling dips helping recovery, traders said.
March Brent last traded 12 cents up at $22.46 a barrel up from a low of $22.31 that was triggered by the WTI weakness, but well off the days high of $22.80.
"sentiment was mainly influenced by the NYMEX markets," one broker said.
Gas oil futures closed weaker pulled down by weakness in NYMEX crude which coloured the whole energy complex.
The February contract closed down 75 cents at $203.25 a tonne having achieved a high of $207.25 around mid-morning.

"The U.S lost it and pulled everything down with it," said one IPE floor trader. NYMEX selling was mainly technically-led and a recovery was anticipated by dealers as sellers secured their profits and covered their shorts.
Strong end of close selling also contributed bearish pressure, limiting gas oil's room to manoeuvre to a healthy end.
Attention remained focused on the American Petroleum Institute (API) stock data, which is due to be released later on Wednesday.
A consensus of trader estimates pegs the average gasoline stock build at 1.7 million barrels while the average estimate for crude stocks was a build of 1.5 million barrels.
Last week's frigid temperatures in the key heating oil market of the U.S. Northeast heightened heat demand, and is expected to have pushed down distillate stocks around three million barrels.
Estimates were between down two and four million barrels.
While refineries are using less crude and producing less refined product due to the seasonal maintenance, imports from Europe are boosting crude and gasoline stocks, traders said.
